results.title: Using Milestones in Gantt
results.content: You are here: Using the Application>Gantt>Managing Project Tasks in Gantt>Using Milestones in Gantt To display a milestone in Gantt, you need to create a milestone and synchronize it with a project task. When synchronized, the milestone's target date and the task's end date are linked. Changes to one of these values is reflected in the other value. To use milestones in Gantt: You do not need to have a project task selected. The Project Milestones dialog opens and existing milestones are displayed. 2. Add a milestone and enter its details. 3. To create a project task for an existing or new milestone, click Create Task. A project task for the milestone is added below the selected task in the task grid. If you have selected the project or a parent task in the task grid, the project task is added to the bottom of the relevant task list. If you click in the Synchronized Task field, the task and milestone are desynchronized. This removes the link between the task's end date and the milestone's target date. Changes are no longer reflected between these values. When you change a milestone target date outside Gantt, the end date of the synchronized task is updated when the project is next loaded or reloaded in Gantt. Milestone dates might also be updated due to the work calendar. \*\*Note:\*\*When you save the project in Gantt, the project is reloaded when the Gantt preference Reload on saveThis is selected by default. When applied, Gantt reloads data automatically every time that you click Save. results.title: Export the Assignments Gantt - Procore
results.content: # Export the Assignments Gantt. ## Objective. To export the Assignments Gantt in Resource Planning. ## Background. The Assignments Gantt allows you to view resource requests and assignments across all projects and people within your company. It also provides a multi-day view from one (1) day up to three (3) years. ## Things to Consider. * Your export reflects what is displayed on the Assignments Gantt at the time you click to export. ## Steps. * Export the Gantt (Legacy) as a PDF_as_a_PDF "Export the Assignments Gantt"). * Export the Gantt as a PDF or CSV. ### Export the Assignments Gantt (Legacy) as a PDF. 1. Navigate to the company's **Resource Planning** tool. 2. Click **Assignments** and select **Gantt (Legacy)**. 3. The export will reflect the Gantt as its configured on your screen. Follow steps to configure your Gantt view:. * Search and Filter the Assignments Gantt. 4. Click the **Export**  icon. 5. Select****Portrait**** or****Landscape****. 6. *Optional:* If you want each project to print on its own page, mark the **Page Break Between Projects**checkbox. **Note:** If a report does not immediately download, you can check the status by navigating to ****Reports**** and ****Queued Downloads.****. ### Export the Assignments Gantt as a PDF or CSV. ##### In Beta. This feature is in beta and available for customers using the Resource Planning tool. 1. Navigate to the company's **Resource Planning** tool. 2. Click **Assignments** and select**Gantt (Beta)**. 3. The export will reflect the Gantt as its configured on your screen. Follow steps to configure your Gantt view:. * Configure the Assignment Gantt View. * Search and Filter the Assignments Gantt. 5. Select **PDF** or **CSV**. * If exporting a PDF, select the **page******size****. 6. Click **Export** to download PDF or CSV. * Search and Filter the Assignments Gantt.

results.title: Create Interactive Gantt Charts in Python with Plotly.Figure_Factory – TheLinuxCode
results.content: Published Time: 2023-12-27T08:39:07+00:00 Create Interactive Gantt Charts in Python with Plotly.Figure_Factory – TheLinuxCode Create Interactive Gantt Charts in Python with Plotly.Figure_Factory By Linux Code / December 27, 2023 Gantt charts provide a useful way to visualize schedules and task timelines for projects. Python‘s Plotly library makes creating these charts easy with the `figure_factory.create_gantt()` function. A Gantt chart displays tasks or activities on a timeline, showing their start, end and duration. * A vertical axis showing tasks or activities * A horizontal axis representing time * Bars stretching horizontally from the start to end of each task * Visualize project schedules at a glance * Track progress and identify delays * Adjust tasks and schedules easily * Communicate plans clearly to stakeholders Plotly‘s `create_gantt()` function allows building Gantt charts easily from Python. Here‘s a simple example: from plotly.figure_factory import create_gantt dict(Task="Job A", Start=‘2009-01-01‘, Finish=‘2009-02-28‘), dict(Task="Job B", Start=‘2009-03-05‘, Finish=‘2009-04-15‘), dict(Task="Job C", Start=‘2009-02-20‘, Finish=‘2009-05-30‘) This generates the following output: The duration bars stretch automatically based on the Start and Finish dates. Some key parameters of `create_gantt()` include: * `index_col` – Column to use as index * `bar_width` – Width of duration bars * `tasks` – List of task labels Let‘s see how to customize the chart further. from plotly.figure_factory import create_gantt import plotly.graph_objects as go dict(Task=‘Scope‘, Start=‘2023-01-01‘, Finish=‘2023-02-15‘, Complete=100), dict(Task=‘Design‘, Start=‘2023-02-15‘, Finish=‘2023-04-15‘, Complete=60), dict(Task=‘Develop‘, Start=‘2023-04-15‘, Finish=‘2024-01-30‘, Complete=30), dict(Task=‘Test‘, Start=‘2024-01-30‘, Finish=‘2024-03-30‘, Complete=30), dict(Task=‘Deploy‘, Start=‘2024-03-30‘, Finish=‘2024-06-15‘, Complete=0) fig = create_gantt(df, show_colorbar=True, title=‘Project Timeline‘) # Milestones as points x=[df.loc[0, ‘Finish‘], df.loc[1, ‘Finish‘]], marker=dict(size=15, color=‘green‘), This generates an integrated view with milestone markers: The `%b\n%Y` timescale formatting displays meses and years clearly even when zoomed. Plotly‘s `figure_factory.create_gantt()` provides a flexible way to build Gantt charts from Pandas data frames. Some next steps for practicing could be: * Connect charts to live data sources * Experiment with assignments and groups * Integrate completion status and milestones * Deploy interactive Dashboards with Gantt, grid and filters Hopefully this tutorial helps you learn how to effectively harness Plotly‘s Python charting capabilities for project visualizations! Creating Gantt Charts with Plotly Express Timelines 2.
